text: Once upon a time, in the middle of winter, a queen sat sewing by an ebony window.
Snow fell like feathers. She pricked her finger, and three drops of blood fell on the snow.
"If only I had a child," she said, "white as snow, red as blood, and black as ebony."
Her wish came true. But when the girl was born, the queen died, and the king took a new wife.
The new queen was beautiful, and proud. Each morning she asked her magic mirror:
"Mirror, mirror on the wall, who is the fairest of them all?" And for years, the mirror answered: "You are."
But Snow White grew, and by seven she was as beautiful as the day itself. One morning the mirror answered: "You are fair, Queen. But Snow White is fairer still."
The queen's heart filled with envy. She ordered her huntsman to take the child deep into the forest, and not bring her back.
But as he raised his knife, Snow White begged for her life, and his heart would not let him strike. "Run, child," he said. "Run, and never come back."
He brought the queen a boar's heart instead. Snow White ran over stones and through thorns until the light faded.
asr: He brought the Queen a boar's heart instead. Snow white ran over stones and threw thorns until the light faded.

text: In the dark she found a tiny house. Inside, all was small and neat: seven little plates, seven little cups, seven little beds.
Hungry and weary, she tasted from each plate, lay down in the seventh bed, and slept.
At nightfall the owners came home: seven dwarfs who dug for ore in the mountains. They found her asleep, and marvelled at her beauty.
asr: At nightfall the owners came home, seven dwarfs who dug for ore in the mountains, they found her asleep and marveled at her beauty.

text: In the morning she told them everything. "Stay with us," they said. "Keep our house. And beware the queen: let no one in."
But the mirror told the queen Snow White still lived, beyond the seven hills. So the queen disguised herself, and knocked at the cottage door.
First, laces, pulled so tight that Snow White fell as if dead. The dwarfs came home in time, and cut them free.
Then came a poisoned comb. One touch of its teeth, and she fell again. Once more, the dwarfs saved her.
asr: Then came a poisoned comb. One touch of its teeth and she fell again, once more the dwarf saved her.

text: Then the queen made her finest poison: an apple half white, half red, so lovely that anyone who saw it longed for a taste.
asr: Then the queen made her finest poison, an apple half white, half red, so lovely that anyone who saw it longed for taste.

text: "See? I eat it myself," said the queen, and ate the white half. Snow White bit the red, and fell.
This time nothing could wake her. The dwarfs laid her in a glass coffin so all could see her beauty, and kept watch on the hill.
One day a prince rode by. He saw the coffin, read its golden letters, and begged the dwarfs: "Let me take her with me. I cannot live without seeing her."
His servants lifted the coffin, and stumbled on a root. The jolt shook the piece of poisoned apple loose from her throat.
She opened her eyes, lifted the lid, and sat up. "Where am I?" she cried. "You are with me," said the prince.
They were married with great joy. But far away the queen asked her mirror one last question. At the answer she fled into the night, and behind her the mirror cracked.
And Snow White lived happily for many years: white as snow, red as blood, kind as the day she was born.
